title: Thumos Industrials governance and data lifecycle review
topics: SSO / SAML integration and IdP options
Audit logs, retention and immutable logs
Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Introductory security posture review focused on whether Redwood Hosted or a Private/Dedicated deployment meets Thumos' governance and data lifecycle constraints. Key asks: SOC2 and ISO evidence, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC model for multi-team access, KMS/HSM integration, and a data retention/archival plan. Decided next step: Redwood to share docs and an architecture sketch for Private with KMS; customer to share retention policy and schedule a PoC kickoff week of 11/16.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share latest SOC2 report, ISO27001 summary, and pen test high-level findings - due 2026-11-13
Ravi Patel: Produce a Private deployment architecture diagram showing KMS/HSM integration, network diagrams (VPC peering options) and RBAC patterns - due 2026-11-16
Marcus Hale: Send Thumos' data retention table and regulatory constraints (EU residency, 7-year archival requirement) - due 2026-11-12
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 + ISO attestations and compliance pack
Schedule 60-min PoC kickoff (technical) week of 2026-11-16 with SE and Thumos infra
Customer to confirm whether they prefer Private (VPC) or Dedicated reserved capacity before PoC
Ravi to prepare KMS integration options (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, external HSM)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-09 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Thumos Head of Infrastructure), Marcus Hale (Thumos Security Engineer), Priya Reddy (Platform Lead)

Auto-generated Summary: Security posture and data lifecycle intake; customer leaning toward private deployment but evaluating cost and operational burden.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, joining with Ravi our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:34 - Lena Ortiz: Good—morning for some of us, afternoon for others. Quick context: Thumos is moving inference into production for equipment telemetry insights, and security/compliance is the gating factor.
01:10 - Maya Chen: Great. Today we wanted to walk through your governance constraints, what evidence you need (SOC2 / ISO), and map possible deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.
01:45 - Marcus Hale: The big things for us: SOC2 attestation, SSO via our IdP (we use Okta), RBAC around teams, audit logging that's immutable and exportable, plus encryption keys under our control. Also data retention rules — we have a 7-year retention for certain records and EU residency for some customers.
02:20 - Ravi Patel: Understood. We can support SAML SSO/Okta, offer RBAC primitives, and for keys we have two modes: Redwood-managed KMS for hosted, or customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private/Dedicated. For on-prem we can integrate with external HSMs.
03:05 - Priya Reddy: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private? I think earlier material blurred them for us.
03:40 - Maya Chen: Sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's environment with tenant isolation and contractual guarantees — you still use Redwood's control plane. Private means a customer VPC or on-prem control plane where you control networking and KMS — more isolation and control but higher ops surface.
04:10 - Marcus Hale: So if we need our keys in an HSM, that's only possible with Private or some Dedicated variants?
04:35 - Ravi Patel: Correct. For strict HSM/BYOK we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem). There are some Dedicated options where you can bring your KMS through a dedicated customer key escrow model, but it depends on the provider and contract.
05:05 - Speaker 1: (inaudible) ... cost implications?
05:22 - Maya Chen: Good point. Private usually carries more upfront integration work and potentially higher monthly costs, but it reduces egress/PII concerns and meets stricter compliance. Dedicated sits in the middle: predictable cost but less operational overhead than fully private.
06:00 - Lena Ortiz: Our compliance team will want SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 evidence, pen test summaries, and network diagrams. Can you provide those?
06:28 - Maya Chen: Yes, we can share the SOC2 report redacted for public distribution, ISO summary, and a security pack. We'll redact any customer-specific data.
06:55 - Marcus Hale: About audit logs: we need immutable logs retained for 5 years and ability to stream to our SIEM (Splunk). Is that doable?
07:20 - Ravi Patel: We have an export pipeline — logs can be exported to S3 or streamed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder. Immutability is achievable by writing to WORM enabled S3 buckets or your own logging infra.
07:55 - Priya Reddy: What about token-level or prompt-level logging? We can't retain raw prompts for more than 30 days for some customers.
08:20 - Maya Chen: You can configure retention policies per data class. Redwood supports configurable retention and can mask or not store prompt text depending on the deployment. In Private you get more control over storage policies.
09:00 - Lena Ortiz: KMS question: we run AWS KMS with multi-account setup. Do you support cross-account KMS or do we need to provision keys in Redwood account?
09:30 - Ravi Patel: For Private, you bring keys to your VPC or you can configure cross-account key usage via IAM roles and key policies. For hosted, we'd use Redwood-managed keys unless you choose BYOK with supported providers. We'll document specifics for AWS, GCP, and Azure.
10:05 - Marcus Hale: Encryption at rest for model artifacts — who has access to the unencrypted model?
10:30 - Ravi Patel: In hosted, Redwood's runtime needs access in memory during inference; keys for disk encryption are managed per deployment. In Private you control the encryption layer and HSM if desired.
11:00 - Speaker 2: (overlap) ... question on RBAC...
11:16 - Maya Chen: On RBAC, Redwood supports role-based policies: admin, developer, observer, and custom roles through the Console and API. For Private we can map to your IdP groups via SCIM sync.
11:45 - Priya Reddy: SCIM would be ideal. We want group sync from Okta and attribute-based access control for environments.
12:10 - Ravi Patel: We can do SCIM + SAML and map Okta groups to RBAC roles; we'll include examples in the architecture doc.
12:38 - Lena Ortiz: Audit trail — do you capture token usage linked to user identity for forensics?
13:00 - Maya Chen: Token and request-level metadata can be correlated to user identity with SSO and API key mapping. We keep trace IDs to tie back to requests; retention windows are configurable.
13:40 - Marcus Hale: Any third-party assessments? SOC vendors, pen testers?
14:00 - Maya Chen: We run annual pen tests and third-party vulnerability scans. We'll share redacted summaries; full reports can be handled under an NDA.
14:35 - Priya Reddy: Data residency — for EU customers we need hosting in eu-west-1. Does Redwood support regional hosting for Private?
15:00 - Ravi Patel: Yes, Private deployments can be in your cloud region or on-prem. Hosted API has region options, and we can pin inference workloads to EU regions to meet residency.
15:40 - Speaker 3: (muted background)
16:05 - Lena Ortiz: On retention: some records must be archived for 7 years and not be purgeable by day-to-day operators. Can you support that?
16:30 - Ravi Patel: For Private, you control storage lifecycle and access controls; we recommend using write-once storage for archival data or separate archival buckets with restricted access. For Hosted we can implement retention rules but operational controls are less customer-managed.
17:10 - Marcus Hale: Are logs tamper-evident? We need proof-of-integrity for audit.
17:35 - Maya Chen: We support checksuming and can recommend a process using signed manifests and WORM-enabled storage; we'll include sample configs.
18:05 - Priya Reddy: Wanted to flag latency/cost tradeoff — model choices and quantization affect inference cost. If we go Private we still want Redwood's Optimize recommendations to keep token costs reasonable.
18:40 - Ravi Patel: Absolutely — Optimize is part of our tooling and can run with Private deployments; we'll include tuning recommendations and cost modeling in the doc bundle.
19:15 - Lena Ortiz: What's the SLA for Dedicated vs Private? We need at least 99.9% for inference endpoints for the production tier.
19:40 - Maya Chen: Dedicated can come with SLA terms in the contract (99.9% typical), Private SLA depends on whether you're on-prem or customer-managed — Redwood can provide an SLA for the control plane if hosted in our managed private offering.
20:10 - Marcus Hale: For SAML flows, we insist on SP-initiated and IdP-initiated with enforced session timeouts and forced MFA. Can you enforce session policies?
20:35 - Ravi Patel: We support SAML with configurable session durations, and you can enforce MFA at the IdP level. We'll document recommended session timeout defaults and how to configure them via Okta.
21:05 - Speaker 1: (brief) ... integration timelines?
21:20 - Maya Chen: For a standard Private PoC we typically run a 4-week technical validation: week 0 on-boarding, week 1 integration (SSO/KMS), week 2 workload testing and logging integration, week 3 runbench/latency and cost tuning.
22:00 - Priya Reddy: Who does the work: Redwood or our infra? We have limited ops headcount.
22:20 - Ravi Patel: For Private there's a shared responsibility model. Redwood assists with the control plane and runtime integration; the customer handles cloud networking, KMS provisioning, and certain infra tasks. We can provide an onboarding runbook and professional services to accelerate.
23:00 - Marcus Hale: If we require HSM-backed keys, what's the onboarding lead time?
23:20 - Ravi Patel: Onboarding with HSM can add 2-4 weeks depending on procurement and key policies. We'll give a checklist.
24:00 - Lena Ortiz: About evidence: can Redwood provide access logs and sample log schema for our SOC team to review?
24:22 - Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include log schema, sample event payloads, and export instructions.
24:45 - Priya Reddy: What about long-term storage costs for logs and embeddings? Embeddings retention could be seasonal and large.
:25:10 - Ravi Patel: We'll include cost estimates for cold storage vs hot storage and recommendations for TTL on embeddings; also options to store embeddings encrypted under your KMS.
25:45 - Speaker 2: (background) ...
26:10 - Marcus Hale: For legal/comms, we need data flow diagrams showing which party processes what and where PII resides.
26:35 - Maya Chen: We'll produce a simplified data flow diagram and a table of processing roles for each component.
27:05 - Lena Ortiz: If we go with Hosted initially, how hard is it to later migrate to Private or Dedicated?
27:30 - Ravi Patel: We design for migration: model artifacts and prompts can be staged; there are some considerations around key material and replayable caches, but a migration path is supported with planning.
28:05 - Priya Reddy: Would you be able to sign an addendum around data retention?
28:30 - Maya Chen: We can attach contractual language around retention and deletion policies as part of the enterprise agreement. We'll loop legal on that.
29:00 - Marcus Hale: Any known incidents in the last two years impacting data retention or exfil?
29:20 - Maya Chen: No client-impacting incidents to disclose. We'll include our incident history summary in the security pack.
29:55 - Lena Ortiz: On monitoring — can we pull request traces into our APM for latency analysis?
30:15 - Ravi Patel: Yes we support trace hooks and can forward traces or provide integrations with common APMs.
31:00 - Speaker 4: (soft)
31:20 - Priya Reddy: For compliance, do you provide SOC2 scoping guidance? Some of our services are in-scope and some are not.
31:40 - Maya Chen: We can share our SOC2 scope and advise on what parts of integration would fall in-scope for Thumos. We'll plan a session with our compliance lead if needed.
32:10 - Marcus Hale: We may want a joint architecture review with our security team and Redwood SEs.
32:35 - Maya Chen: Happy to set that up — SE-led deep dive to map controls to your policy.
33:05 - Lena Ortiz: On retention again — we also need proof of deletion workflow for when a record needs to be removed under GDPR; how is deletion handled in Private vs Hosted?
33:30 - Ravi Patel: In Private you control delete pipelines and can verify deletions; in Hosted we provide deletion APIs and can perform deletion workflows, plus attestations for deletion events.
34:00 - Priya Reddy: Is there a sandbox to test deletion behavior?
34:20 - Ravi Patel: Yes we provide test environments and can simulate retention rules.
34:50 - Maya Chen: Quick recap: We'll send compliance pack, SOC2/ISO summaries, sample logs and diagram, and an architecture sketch for Private with KMS. We'll propose a PoC schedule week of 11/16.
35:20 - Marcus Hale: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Procuring ephemeral infra and scheduling will be the main ones.
35:40 - Lena Ortiz: Also need to decide whether Defense business will require on-prem; that's pending.
36:05 - Priya Reddy: For the PoC can we get a cost estimate ballpark for 4-week Private PoC?
36:30 - Ravi Patel: We'll include a cost worksheet with reserved GPU estimates and staff hours.
37:00 - Speaker 5: (keyboard)
37:20 - Maya Chen: We'll also add recommended RBAC mappings and SCIM config examples for Okta.
37:45 - Marcus Hale: If we go forward, who's point of contact?
38:00 - Maya Chen: I'll be the commercial owner; Ravi is the SE for tech. We'll introduce a solutions engineer and a compliance contact if needed.
38:25 - Lena Ortiz: Can you include a minimal SSO test plan for our IdP team to run?
38:45 - Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll add a runbook with test steps and expected responses.
39:10 - Priya Reddy: Any constraints on IP access lists? We need to lock inbound access to certain CIDR ranges.
39:30 - Ravi Patel: For Private, we can setup VPC peering or private link and restrict inbound CIDRs. For Hosted, we can restrict via token scopes and network allowlists per customer.
40:05 - Marcus Hale: Final question — who hosts model weights if we use third-party open models? Where is the canonical copy?
40:30 - Maya Chen: Model weights are stored in Redwood-managed object storage for hosted by default; for Private you can allow weights to be stored in your buckets and we can pull them into the runtime without persisting in Redwood's storage if that's a requirement. We'll include a model storage options table.
41:05 - Lena Ortiz: Excellent. Thank you.
41:20 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll recap action items shortly.
41:40 - (short silence)
42:00 - Maya Chen: Quick run through of next steps: I'll send docs, Ravi will prepare architecture, Marcus to send retention policy. We'll aim to get PoC scheduled.
42:30 - Marcus Hale: I'll get retention and speak with legal about NDA for full pen test reports.
43:00 - Priya Reddy: We'll review the compliance pack and follow up with questions.
43:30 - Maya Chen: Great. We'll circulate meeting notes with links to the security pack and PoC sign-up.
44:00 - (wrap up)
47:58 - Call ended

Questions (auto):
- Do you need a dedicated SLA for inference endpoints? (Yes, customer requested 99.9%+)
- Which KMS/HSM providers are supported? (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, external HSM via PKCS#11/CloudHSM)
- Is SCIM supported for Okta group sync? (Yes)

References mentioned: compliance pack link (to be shared), sample architecture diagram (to be shared), cost worksheet (to be shared). Some transcription artifacts present (occasional mislabels, brief inaudible segments).
